item.description:
Dominion of the Spear is a very simple set of wargames rules allowing one to fight two armies (pre gunpowder) against each other in just a few minutes. Although figures can be used, battles can easily be fought on paper (no measuring) using pen or pencil and two different coloured six sided dice. 196 army lists are included divided into the periods: the Ancient Near East Age, Age of the Greek and Persian Wars, Age of the Romans, the Dark Ages, Age of the Crusaders, Age of Mongol Invasions and the Late Middle Ages. Armies consist of 3-6 units or commands and the points system is included. There is a complete play through of the Battle of Hydaspes 326 BC between Alexander the Great and King Porus of India.
Designer Notes are included along with a quick reference sheet on the back cover.
from the designer: The armies are deployed as left flank, centre, and right flank with extra units in the reserve. Then combat in each of these three sectors are resolved sector by sector. A six sided dice is used for each unit to hit and rout it's opponent with missile armed units firing first. Defeated units are replaced from the reserve. The fun and interest comes from the interaction of the different types of units with missile mounted units having an advantage over melee infantry, melee infantry having an advantage over missile infantry, missile infantry over melee mounted, and melee mounted over missile mounted. Then there are outflanking bonuses. A battle can be fought in around 10 minutes or less and with some imagination generates an amusing story. Brief rules are given for scaling up with a bigger battlefield and bigger armies. Really designed to be played solo.

Dominion of the Stars is a solitaire game in which you take the role of a world empire expanding its sovereignty into space. This calls for sending starships from your home planet to explore deep space. Along the way you will make various discoveries while trying to colonize as many planets as possible. Colonization of a planet is achieved after its discovery, conquest, and development have taken place. In addition, you must retain control of your planets by protecting them from the game-controlled enemy race.
Planet Discovery Dominion of the Stars takes place in a fictitious galaxy where many formidable findings await. Among your findings will be planets requiring commitment and investment if you hope to colonize them. Assessing a planet’s profile requires the determination of the following key data:
• The value of the planet’s natural resources.
• The presence of intelligent lifeforms.
• The difficulty of development/colonization.
Quadrant Accessibility At the onset, the only major discovery is a WarpGate located within your home quadrant. A WarpGate provides instantaneous travel to other quadrants. As more WarpGates are discovered, more quadrants become accessible. The game provides a total of 7 quadrants that can be explored based on access.
Starship Movement Normal space travel is performed using hex-to-hex movement. In addition to moving from hex to hex, a player may move from level to level (within a hex). Hex level is represented by counter placement; how a counter is orientated or whether it is inverted.
Starship Types The player oversees the following types of starships on behalf of the empire:
• Exploration starships –used to discover habitable planets in deep space (among other discoveries).
• Military starships --used to secure fleets during exploration, and to conquer/defend planets.
• Development starships -- used on one-way missions, these starships are necessary for colonizing planets.
Winning/Losing There are different degrees of win and loss as outlined by the Achievement Scale. Through the process of discovering and controlling planets, it is possible to win the game. If you are unable to discover and control the necessary number of planets by the end of 26 turns, the game is lost.
Dominion of the Stars is available as a free Print & Play game (uploaded to BGG) or as a Print-on-Demand (see official link). In the Print & Play version, counters replace all the non-cardboard pieces (except for the rolling dice).
